title: 白教堂的雾 — 开膛手杰克 (1888) · 抖音竖屏 3 分钟

shots.prompt: Slow dolly forward along a narrow fog-choked Whitechapel street at night, a single cast-iron gas lamp flickering amber, fog drifting in layers across the frame, wet cobblestones glistening, soot-stained brick warehouses, distant church spire; at the far end of the street a tall silhouette holding a lantern crosses the road and dissolves into the fog. No faces visible. Camera: slow push in, slight handheld drift.

Low angle looking up at a soot-blackened Victorian brick tenement at night, laundry lines swaying, a single candle-lit window on the third floor where a thin woman with grey hair in a bun draws a curtain closed; fog rolls past the chimney pots; the gas lamp below flickers. Camera: slow tilt down from the roofline to the wet street.

Extreme close-up of a gloved hand dipping a steel-nib pen into a bottle of red ink on a scarred wooden desk lit by a single candle; the nib touches cream paper and begins writing in looping Victorian script; ink bleeds slightly into the paper fibres; candle flame trembles. Camera: static macro, shallow focus, the flame flicker animates the shadows.

A stocky middle-aged carman with a thick brown moustache, flat cap and canvas work jacket walks toward camera down Buck's Row at 3:40 AM, swinging a tin lantern that throws swaying light across the brick wall; his breath fogs in the cold; he slows and squints ahead. Camera: tracking backward at walking pace, lantern light swinging.

Over-the-shoulder of the moustached carman in a flat cap as he raises his lantern toward the base of a gateway; the light reveals only a dark bundle of shawl and skirt lying against the wall in deep shadow, a woman's boot, a fallen straw bonnet; fog drifts between him and the gate. Camera: slow push in past his shoulder, everything beyond the boot stays in shadow, no wounds, no face.

Medium close-up of the carman's weathered face lit from below by his lantern: thick brown moustache, broad nose, deep-set eyes, realistic proportions; he stares at something off-frame below, his jaw tightens, he slowly takes off his flat cap and swallows; restrained dread, no exaggeration; fog curls behind him. Camera: very slow push in.

High angle looking down into a cramped Hanbury Street backyard at dawn: a dozen East Enders crowd the fence and doorway — an old woman in a shawl, a barefoot boy, a bearded docker, a young red-haired woman with a baby, a bald man in an apron — all different faces, shifting, craning to see; grey dawn light, mist in the yard; two constables in tall helmets hold them back. Camera: slow descending crane.

A tall detective inspector in his forties with a heavy dark walrus moustache, receding hairline, black bowler hat and long grey overcoat steps out of a back door into the misty yard, removes his hat, and slowly scans the scene with tired, intelligent eyes; behind him constables' helmets bob; dawn light through fog. Camera: slow arc around him at eye level.

Close-up of the inspector's gloved hand resting on a rough wooden fence, rainwater dripping from the slats; slow rack focus from his hand to a row of grimy back windows where several different faces — a young girl, an old man with a clay pipe, a woman with a lace cap — watch silently from behind the glass, breath fogging the panes. Camera: rack focus, then slow pan across the windows.

Top-down shot of a Central News Agency desk: a clerk's ink-stained hands with rolled shirt sleeves open a cream envelope and unfold a letter written in red ink; the looping script fills the frame; a brass desk lamp casts a warm pool of light; a teacup steams; papers stir in a draught. Camera: slow push in toward the red writing.

A young clerk with round wire spectacles, neat side-parted blond hair and a starched collar reads the red-ink letter under a green-shaded desk lamp; his eyebrows rise, he glances nervously over his shoulder toward a dark doorway, then back at the page; the lamp flame flickers. Camera: slow push in on his face.

A Victorian steam printing press thundering in a dim pressroom: giant iron rollers spin, sheets of newsprint fly off in a blur, a soot-faced pressman with a grey beard and leather apron pulls a lever; sparks and steam; the printed pages are a soft out-of-focus grey blur with no legible words. Camera: fast tracking shot along the press.

A freckled newsboy of about ten in an oversized cap and patched jacket stands on a foggy street corner under a gas lamp waving a newspaper above his head and shouting, mouth open, breath steaming; well-dressed passers-by in top hats and bonnets turn their heads and snatch copies; horse-drawn cab wheels splash past. Camera: slow push in through the crowd toward the boy.

Berner Street at 1 AM: a small pony pulling a costermonger's cart suddenly shies and rears at a dark gateway, nostrils flaring, eyes rolling white; the driver — a thin man with a black beard and wide-brimmed hat — hauls on the reins, half-standing; the gateway beyond is pitch black; fog swirls. Camera: handheld, slight shake, low angle on the frightened pony.

Continuous lateral tracking shot along a fog-filled London street: gas lamps pass one by one like ghostly halos, dark house fronts slide by, the fog thickens into a solid white wall, and the camera pushes through it to emerge in a wide empty square lined with dark arcades. No people. Camera: smooth lateral dolly then push through fog.

A young constable in a tall custodian helmet and rain cape, clean-shaven with a strong jaw and pale worried eyes, walks slowly into Mitre Square holding a bullseye lantern; the beam sweeps across the wet flagstones, passes a dark corner, stops, and slowly returns to it; he freezes. Camera: following behind him, then slow push past his shoulder toward the dark corner, nothing explicit shown.

A dark tenement doorway on Goulston Street lit by a policeman's lantern: on the black brick wall a line of chalk writing in a scrawled hand glows in the beam; a torn scrap of cloth lies on the step; the lantern beam wavers; fog drifts through the doorway. Camera: slow push in on the chalk letters, the letters remain out of focus and illegible.

Close-up: a gentleman's hand in a white cuff with a gold cufflink, holding a wet sponge, wipes across a smudge of white chalk marks on dark brick; the marks are an illegible blur that smears and vanishes in streaks; water runs down the wall; behind, out of focus, a stern grey-whiskered police commissioner in a peaked cap watches. Camera: static close on the wall, slight drift.

A cluster of Victorian policemen's faces in a dark doorway lit from below by a single lantern — a young one with freckles, a sergeant with mutton-chop whiskers, an older one with a scar over his eyebrow, a stout one with a red nose — realistic human proportions, painterly realism, each face different; they exchange uneasy glances as the light flickers and shadows swing across them; dawn greys the sky behind. Camera: slow pan across the faces.

Miller's Court, a squalid brick courtyard on a grey November morning: a nervous young man with a thin face, prominent ears and a shabby brown coat knocks on a peeling green door of number 13, waits, knocks again, then leans toward a small window with a broken pane covered by a curtain. Camera: slow push in behind him.

Close-up on the thin young man's face as he reaches through the broken pane and lifts the edge of a muslin curtain; faint firelight from inside flickers across his cheek and eyes; his eyes widen, pupils shrink, his mouth opens, colour drains from his face. Nothing inside is shown. Camera: slow push in on his eyes.

The young man stumbles backward from the window into the courtyard, knocks over a wooden bucket that clatters and rolls, and runs out through the narrow arched passage toward the street; the green door remains shut; a crow lifts off the roof; a curtain in the window falls still. Camera: static wide, then slow push toward the closed door.

A dark gallery wall: a candle carried by an unseen hand moves along a row of oil portraits, illuminating each in turn — a gaunt Polish barber with hollow cheeks and wild dark hair; a handsome young barrister with fair side whiskers; a florid American doctor with a huge grey moustache; a sharp-faced painter with a pointed beard — four completely different faces; each fades back into darkness as the light passes. Camera: smooth lateral tracking with the candle.

The candlelight reaches the last frame on the dark gallery wall: an ornate gilded frame whose canvas is completely blank and black, no picture and no face inside it, only cracked dark varnish; the flame trembles, throws long shadows, then gutters; the empty frame slowly sinks into darkness. Camera: slow push in on the empty frame.

Inside a Scotland Yard archive: a wooden card-index drawer slides open by itself, yellowed case files flip open, pages lift and turn in a draught, dust motes drift in a shaft of pale light; a magnifying glass rests on a faded floral silk shawl. Camera: slow push in over the drawer toward the magnifying glass.

Extreme close-up through a magnifying glass of the woven silk fibres of an old faded floral shawl; the threads begin to glow and rearrange themselves into a slowly rotating luminous double helix painted in amber and slate-blue brushstrokes against darkness, then dissolve back into fog and thread; no people, no faces. Camera: slow rotation, painterly transition.

The same narrow Whitechapel street as the opening: the fog thins and lifts, night turns to grey morning, the gas lamp gutters out, translucent ghostly figures of modern passers-by stream through the frame at high speed like long-exposure trails, the brick walls stay unchanged; painterly time-lapse. Camera: static locked-off, matching the opening framing.

The empty foggy Whitechapel street at dusk: one dark figure in a long coat and top hat stands far down the street with his back to camera under the last lit gas lamp; he slowly begins to turn his head toward the camera, but the fog thickens and swallows him before his face is revealed; the lamp flickers out. Camera: very slow push in, ending in near-darkness.
